note: The .lzma (LZMA alone) format over lzma1 0.6.1 (a port of XZ for Java), where CyberChef uses lzma-js. Compression Mode is the level parameter with the same 1 to 9 range and CyberChef's default of 7; there is no level 0, because the format has no store mode. The 13-byte header and the output are the same format, so xz --format=lzma, 7-Zip and Python's lzma module read the output, but the bytes differ from CyberChef's (a different encoder), and the outputs are pinned to lzma1 0.6.1. Out-of-range levels are E_RANGE.

The .lzma format, with no options, as CyberChef's operation has none. Output is the same bytes CyberChef gives for a valid stream. The header is checked (a short header or a properties byte out of range is E_COERCE), and a declared size above the value limit is E_LIMIT_VALUE before anything is decoded. An unknown size (all 0xFF) is decoded only up to the limit: more output is E_LIMIT_VALUE, the decompression bomb rule of the wave 6 conventions. Truncated, corrupt data, and output whose length differs from the declared size, are E_COERCE.
